verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into his E-W-R combo around levels 3-8; you win if you deny those windows and scale into tank items, where the matchup sits at 58.6% over 70 games.

brief.thesis: Jax's entire threat is condensed into short windows: E (Counter Strike) dodges your autos and then stuns on expiry, W (Empower) buffs his next hit, and once he's 6 his R (Relentless Assault) stacks attack speed for free on every strike. Ornn has no auto-attack reliance to punish and instead wins by CC-chaining Q into E for a knockup while his Living Forge tankiness and masterwork items make extended fights (not short trades) his domain. The lane is even on paper, but Ornn's structural win condition is patience, not poke.

theirWindow.when: His E and W (Empower) both up
theirWindow.what: He can dodge your autos, land an empowered hit, and stun on E's expiry. Do not trade basic attacks in this window; only your Q (Volcanic Rupture) and E (Searing Charge) still land cleanly since they aren't basic attacks.

yourWindow.when: His E (Counter Strike) just went down
yourWindow.what: E sits on an 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown. The moment it's spent, slow him with Q then charge E into the nearest wall for the knockup, chaining Q again while he has no stun or dodge to answer with.

start.why: Hits 61.3% over 31 games in this matchup; the block-on-hit and regen directly answer Jax's early auto-attack poke without needing to commit to a trade.

boots.why: 73.3% pick, 57.1% win rate; flat damage reduction on autos cuts into both his basic attack poke and his R-fueled attack speed scaling later.

core.why: Sustained AoE burn pressures him off trades and starts building the tank base before his level 6-8 all-in window closes.
Directly punishes an auto-attack-reliant kit; every stacked R hit he lands returns damage and the grievous wounds cuts any sustain he picks up.
Completes the core build path seen in measured games, giving stacking resistances that scale Ornn's advantage the longer the fight runs.

situational.when: the enemy team stacks attack speed or crit the same way Jax's kit does
you need an active slow to shut down dives or his Q (Leap Strike) engage
the enemy composition shifts toward heavy burst magic damage
Jax or his team builds meaningful lifesteal or sustain healing

runes.keystoneWhy: The proc-and-heal rewards landing a Q/E chain in melee range rather than trading autos, and the sustain outlasts Jax's short poke windows instead of racing his burst.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 73.1% of games; Teleport lets you reset for Sunfire/Thornmail components and still return to lane, which matters since the matchup is won on item timing, not early kills. Flash+Ignite (66.7% win rate) is a viable alternative if you want to punish his weaker levels 1-2 directly.

playing.title: Bait autos, not abilities
playing.detail: Never trade basic attacks into Jax while his E (Counter Strike) is active, since it dodges all basic attacks; your Q (Volcanic Rupture) fissure and slow still land cleanly.

playing.title: All-in right after his E
playing.detail: His E sits on an 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown. Once it's down, land Q then charge E (Searing Charge) into terrain for the knockup chain.

playing.title: Step off empowered autos
playing.detail: His W (Empower, cd 7/6/5/4/3s) buffs his next hit; when it pops, back out of his 300-range window instead of absorbing the bonus damage.

playing.title: Respect level 6 all-in
playing.detail: Once he hits 6, R (Relentless Assault) gives free stacking attack speed on every strike; play for Q poke, not extended autos, until Sunfire/Thornmail are online.

playing.title: Punish his only gap closer
playing.detail: Jax's Q (Leap Strike) is his sole engage tool, as low as a 5s cooldown at max rank; if he leaps in, answer with E into terrain to knock him up.

playing.title: Freeze for your item timing
playing.detail: The lane is even with a solo-kill edge to Jax early, so don't overextend for CS before Thornmail and Sunfire Aegis complete; those are the items that flip the matchup.

playing.title: Use R to finish, not open
playing.detail: Ornn's R (Call of the Forge God, cd 140/120/100/100/100s) is far slower than his 0s R; summon it to follow up a knockup or zone a fight rather than opening blind, since whiffing it leaves you without your biggest CC for minutes.

brief.patchCaveat: The build paths, boots, runes, summoner spells, and every win-rate/sample-size figure above are pulled directly from OP.GG's measured games on the current patch; the trade-timing and ability-interaction reasoning is my own tactical read, not measured data.
